title: SLO entanglement mitigation and cross-team activation plan
content:
Summary:
This doc defines a pragmatic activation plan to identify, triage, and mitigate SLO entanglement across product and infra teams. "SLO entanglement" means multiple services, routes, or policies whose SLOs interact in ways that cause surprising error budgets, cascading throttles, or oscillating rollouts. The goal is to reduce incident surface area caused by these interactions and to create a repeatable handoff pattern for feature teams and platform owners.

Background and motivation:
- Over the last 6 months we've observed a recurring pattern: a high-throughput, low-latency path (hosted-api) and a bursty background batch worker share a caching layer + routing policy. When batch runs spike, it consumes capacity and pushes the hosted API into error budget burn, triggering emergency rollbacks and throttles.
- Current ownership is fuzzy: product owns feature latency SLO; infra owns capacity & routing; platform owns caching. No single owner looks end-to-end.
- Business impact: repeated rollbacks increase customer-visible latency, raise support tickets, and obscure real reliability signals.

Objective (measurable):
1) Establish a standard SLO entanglement discovery checklist and taxonomy across three pilot services within 8 weeks.
2) Reduce cascading error-budget-triggered rollbacks by 50% for pilot services within 12 weeks.
3) Create a cross-team activation runbook and onboarding checklist so future features declare entanglement risks at design review.

Scope:
- In scope: hosted-api routes, shared caching layer, routing policies, autoscaling groups, and background batch pipelines that share GPU/CPU pools.
- Out of scope: unrelated internal tools, customer-managed private deployments (unless customer-specific SLOs are involved).

Roles & stakeholders:
- SRE lead (project sponsor): Aisha Patel — program owner and facilitator.
- Platform owner (cache & routing): Marco Chen — responsible for implementing quick policy fixes and capacity baselines.
- Product partners: Elena Ruiz (hosted-api product manager) — coordinates feature teams for pilot services.
- Observability SME: Danielle O'Leary — defines dashboards, alert rules, and correlation queries.
- Solutions eng / PS contact: Ravi Kumar — customer impact liaison for enterprise-facing services.
- Pilot feature teams: 3 teams identified (payment-ingest, embeddings-indexer, chat-router).

Success metrics (KPIs):
- Number of entanglement incidents per month (baseline measured over prior 3 months).
- Time-to-identify (TTI) entanglement root cause (target: reduce median by 40%).
- % of features with entanglement risk declared at design review (target: 80% for pilot teams).
- Change in error budget burn correlation coefficient between services (target: decrease correlation by 0.3).

Approach (high level):
Phase A — Discover (weeks 0–2):
- Run the SLO entanglement checklist for each pilot service (see Appendix A).
- Produce a dependency graph (manual + automated via traces) showing shared resources and overlapping request windows.
- Short daily sync (15m) with pilot owners to log findings.

Phase B — Quantify (weeks 2–4):
- Instrument cross-service correlation queries (example: sliding-window token burn correlation, request-latency cross-correlation).
- Create a small dashboard per pilot showing: per-route SLO burn, shared-cache hit rate, autoscaler actions, and request origin tags.
- Run controlled load experiments (100% native workload + 2x batch spike) in staging to observe behavior.

Phase C — Mitigate & Activate (weeks 4–8):
- Apply low-effort mitigations: routing isolation for high-priority routes, request rate caps on batch jobs, cache partitioning flags, and KV prefix blacklisting during peak windows.
- For each mitigation, create an A/B rollback plan and a canary gate.
- Update SLOs or create derived SLOs where appropriate (e.g., hosted-api-critical-route SLO tightened; batch-window SLO separate).

Phase D — Operationalize (weeks 8–12):
- Publish cross-team activation runbook and add entanglement checklist to design-review templates.
- Train oncall rotations on triage steps and add entanglement play to incident runbooks.
- Post-mortem and retro for pilot services; feed learnings back to product & platform planning.

SLO entanglement taxonomy (quick):
- Resource contention entanglement: shared GPU/CPU/persistent cache creating direct competition.
- Temporal entanglement: periodic jobs aligning and causing transient overload.
- Routing entanglement: policies route to same pool; low-priority traffic cannibalizes high-priority capacity.
- Observability entanglement: metrics/alerts aggregated in ways that mask underlying independent failures.

Triage workflow (short):
1) Detect: alert triggered, SRE oncall adds "possible entanglement" tag if multiple services show concurrent burn.
2) Correlate: Observability SME runs correlation queries / example trace joins.
3) Isolate: quickly flip a traffic-split or pause batch pipeline (preapproved emergency action) to confirm directionality.
4) Escalate: if isolation confirms entanglement, notify platform + product owners and open REDWOOD-ENTANGLE ticket.
5) Mitigate: apply pre-approved mitigations (routing caps, cache partitioning).
6) Post-incident: record root cause, mitigation timeline, and update SLO docs.

Activation playbook (taskable items):
- Checklist item: "Has team mapped shared resources?" Owner: feature team. Due: week 1.
- Checklist item: "Have cross-service dashboards been created?" Owner: Observability SME. Due: week 2.
- Checklist item: "Is there an emergency pause mechanism for batch jobs?" Owner: Platform. Due: week 3.
- Checklist item: "Can we route high-priority traffic to isolated capacity?" Owner: Infra. Due: week 4.
- Checklist item: "Design review updated to require entanglement declaration." Owner: Product Ops. Due: week 6.

Timeline (milestones):
- Week 0 (kickoff): Alignment meeting, pilot owners confirmed, seeds for dashboards.
- Week 1–2: Discovery checklists completed for 3 pilots; baseline metrics captured.
- Week 3–4: Stage experiments and quantify correlations.
- Week 5–8: Implement mitigations with canary gates.
- Week 9–12: Publish runbook, training, and retro.

Communications & escalation:
- Primary channel: #sre-entanglement (Slack) — use for daily syncs and incident updates.
- Weekly: Reliability digest email to stakeholders with one-liner status and blockers.
- Executive escalation: AVP Eng (cc: Head of Product) if production incidents persist after mitigations.

Dependencies & pre-reqs:
- Observability team must prioritize dashboarding tickets (GH:repo/issue/214).
- Infra needs a temporary quota reserve we can route traffic to for isolation experiments.
- Feature teams must provide two weeks of staging test windows for controlled runs.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Mitigations accidentally reduce capacity for customers. Mitigation: require canary gates + rollback playbooks.
- Risk: Teams slow to adopt design-review change. Mitigation: Product leadership mandate + small incentives (reduced review cycles).

Quick experiments (low-friction):
- Experiment A: Add per-route token bucket limiter for one high-traffic hosted route during batch windows. Measure error budget slope change.
- Experiment B: Partition cache keys by service prefix; compare miss-rate + latency.
- Experiment C: Add synthetic burster in staging to simulate worst-case batch alignment.

Next steps (action items this week):
- Aisha to schedule kickoff with pilot owners (done: invite sent for 2026-05-13).
- Marco to spin up isolated quota pool (GH:infra/ops #598). Due 2026-05-19.
- Danielle to draft 3 baseline dashboards and share links. Due 2026-05-17.

Appendix A — SLO entanglement discovery checklist (one-page):
- Enumerate all SLOs touching the same resource (list routes, queues, batch jobs).
- List shared infra (cache, GPU pool, DB, NAT gateways).
- Identify overlapping schedules or cron windows.
- Check whether alerts are aggregated across services (yes/no).
- Has team validated rollback & pause controls? (documented play).
- Has the team simulated a 2x spike from each dependent service in staging?

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — it favors short experiments and clear ownership. Please call out missing pilots or other entanglement patterns you've seen.

History & provenance:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel 2026-05-12. Minor edits by Marco Chen and Danielle O'Leary 2026-05-19.
